title: Applications of New Hyper Spectral Map Method by Auger Electron Spectroscopy
content: Auger electron spectroscopy (AES) is a famous surface analysis method for elemental/chemical analysis in a minute area of 100 nm2 with a depth of less than 10 nm. It also has a strong ability to acquire an elemental map on the top surface with the high-spatial resolution of several nanometers simultaneously with a secondary electron image. However, its acquisition time is usually about 5 minutes for a wide scan spectrum and about 10 minutes for an elemental map to obtain a good signal-to-noise ratio. The analysis time of AES often becomes a problem for analyzing a complicated surface of an unknown sample because an operator requires significant knowledge and experience in Auger analysis to find all important elements present using several survey spectra obtained after acquisition times of more than 10 minutes. Furthermore, most people must set appropriate energy positions of both peak and backgrounds corresponding to an element of interest whenever an elemental map starts. To overcome these problems, we developed a new hyperspectral map method for AES [1], which we call “Spectrum Image” of Auger (Fig. 1). This new method can provide a special Auger map that includes the electron energy spectrum acquired at each pixel, in data cube format (x, y, electron energy). Therefore, it is possible to extract any spectra in any area, and to reconstruct another trace element map referring to a minor peak that can be hard to find or chemical state map by peak position difference by postprocessing on a user’s PC as they choose.
